correctness.rationale: For the repaired reduced complex locus, work on the monic coefficient chart around any exact (m,m,1^(d−2m)) form. The derivative of multiplication on the product of the two ordered degree-m monic cluster spaces and the residual monic factor has zero kernel by reduction modulo each coprime factor with lower-degree variations. Domain and target dimensions are d, so this is an étale chart. If d=2m, the constant residual factor is omitted. On the open where the factors are mutually coprime and the residual is squarefree, an m-fold root must come from one of the two degree-m factors. Their pure-power loci are smooth graphs with the root recovered from the degree-(m−1) coefficient. In the two independent normal-coordinate blocks they impose (a) or (b), giving the reduced ideal (a)∩(b)=(a_i b_j); the étale pullback is reduced and completions agree at the complex closed point. The q=d−2m+2 free coefficients are the two root parameters and the residual coefficients; each branch has c=m−1 additional parameters and multiplicity one. The restriction sequence to the common regular dimension-q intersection gives depth q+1 because c≥2, and multiplicity associativity gives two. The generic point of the ordered intersection in this algebraic chart maps to the generic point of the stratum closure. Localizing there gives regular branches of dimension c with field intersection, hence depth 1; étale localization has field fiber and preserves dimension and depth. This proves failure of S₂ exactly as claimed in the repaired m≥3 range. The original frozen checker, requirements and recorded output were read, not executed; its tangent-space results and monomial formula checks are bounded support only, and the monomial assertions compare two forms of the same formula.
residual_risks: Only the exact two-designated-root stratum is treated, not any deeper collision, the nonreduced singular scheme, or a global Cohen–Macaulay classification.

Chipalkatti's Theorem 5.4 describes support; §6 discusses arithmetic Cohen–Macaulayness and numerical observations for d≤6, not the generic local depth formula. originality.rationale: For the repaired claim, the strongest accessible primary results characterize normalization fibers, smoothness and singular support, not the independent normal blocks, reduced transverse gluing and exact depths for every m≥3 and d≥2m. Their consequences about two smooth local branches are credited; their number and individual regularity do not specify their mutual contact or local depth. The covered single-cluster cusp and the classical m=2 case were dropped from the finding. No equivalent indexed two-branch/depth result was identified in the bounded comparison.
residual_risks: Weyman's 1993 full text was unavailable. Additional local-algebra consequences there cannot be excluded. The empty external search does not support a claim of exhaustive novelty.

value.rationale: At a natural singular stratum of the standard multiple-root locus, the exact gluing describes the analytic type, multiplicity and failure of S₂ uniformly, including d=2m where there are no residual roots. The exact defect m−2 and the depth-one obstruction off the codimension-one merger locus distinguish features that singular-support and fiber-count descriptions alone do not answer. This is a meaningful local contribution to the Cohen–Macaulay behavior question, not a claim to settle the global problem.
residual_risks: No priority or value credit is attributed to the removed cusp and classical node. Other strata and the parameter ranges where this stratum does not exist are outside the result.
